question.text: How many papers submitted to arXiv in November and December 2026 will mention agentic reinforcement learning in their abstracts?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of search results for "agentic reinforcement learning" occurring in abstracts for papers submitted in the November 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026 time period at arxiv.org. The specific search query to be conducted by Metaculus after December 31, 2026 will be this (but with the dates changed to 2026-11-01 and 2026-12-31): https://arxiv.org/search/advanced?advanced=&terms-0-operator=AND&terms-0-term=%22agentic+reinforcement+learning%22&terms-0-field=abstract&classification-physics_archives=all&classification-include_cross_list=include&date-year=&date-filter_by=date_range&date-from_date=2026-06-01&date-to_date=2026-06-17&date-date_type=submitted_date&abstracts=show&size=200&order=-submitted_date

research:
I couldn't find a forecast on this exact question. The resolution query returned **221** papers for Sep-Oct 2026, the latest two-month window, checked on 2026-11-01. Two quirks of arXiv's search affect any comparison, so I explain them in section 4.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-01: I ran the Metaculus query (abstract contains "agentic reinforcement learning", cross-lists included, filtered by submitted date) on arxiv.org. Counts as of today, by submission window:
  - Sep 1-Oct 31, 2026: **221**
  - Oct 1-31: **138** (Oct 15-31: 71)
  - Sep 1-30: **79**
  - [source](https://arxiv.org/search/advanced?advanced=&terms-0-operator=AND&terms-0-term=%22agentic+reinforcement+learning%22&terms-0-field=abstract&classification-physics_archives=all&classification-include_cross_list=include&date-year=&date-filter_by=date_range&date-from_date=2026-09-01&date-to_date=2026-10-31&date-date_type=submitted_date&abstracts=show&size=50&order=-submitted_date)
- 2026-11-01: The Sep-Oct result list contains many abstracts about classic multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), such as drones, beam control, dispatch and traffic. Those abstracts don't seem to contain the exact phrase "agentic reinforcement learning", so arXiv's phrase matching appears loose (it may treat "agentic" and "multi-agent" alike). For comparison, an exact search for "multi-agent reinforcement learning" returns 87 for Oct 2026, and "agentic RL" returns 38. The count therefore measures more than true agentic-RL papers. [source](https://arxiv.org/search/advanced?advanced=&terms-0-operator=AND&terms-0-term=%22multi-agent+reinforcement+learning%22&terms-0-field=abstract&classification-physics_archives=all&classification-include_cross_list=include&date-year=&date-filter_by=date_range&date-from_date=2026-10-01&date-to_date=2026-10-31&date-date_type=submitted_date&abstracts=show&size=50&order=-submitted_date)
- 2026-11-01: The "submitted date" filter uses each paper's **latest version** date. The October list includes many revisions whose first version dates back to 2023-2025, for example "Submitted 27 October, 2026; v1 submitted 24 June, 2025". So papers revised in Nov-Dec 2026 will count, and papers drop out of older windows when they are revised later. [source](https://arxiv.org/search/advanced?advanced=&terms-0-operator=AND&terms-0-term=%22agentic+reinforcement+learning%22&terms-0-field=abstract&classification-physics_archives=all&classification-include_cross_list=include&date-year=&date-filter_by=date_range&date-from_date=2026-10-01&date-to_date=2026-10-31&date-date_type=submitted_date&abstracts=show&size=200&order=-submitted_date)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-01: The window opens today, so nothing is settled. No Nov-Dec count exists yet.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-01: Tsinghua, Agibot and Wuwen Xinqiong posted a technical report on arXiv about a "Collective Experience Learning" trial with nearly 100 robots. [source](https://www.news.cn/tech/20261101/f57495ef2546436b903f5ab3e51ca554/c.html)
- 2026-10-30: Tech Times reports a Meta FAIR scaling law for training tool-use agents (arXiv, submitted Oct 27). This is the kind of agent-training work that feeds this count. [source](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/329738/20261030/tool-diversity-beats-task-volume-meta-fair-derives-agent-training-scaling-law.htm)
- 2026-10-30: NUS posted DynaFlow, a multi-agent framework paper, on arXiv in October. [source](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/329749/20261030/multi-agent-ai-flaw-information-loss-not-agent-quality-nus-system-fixes-it-code.htm)
- Aug 2026 (arXiv 2608.28612): InternReviewer and InternAdvocate, an agentic RL paper on peer review and rebuttal, shows the term still spreading into new applications. [source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.28612)
- 2026-01: The defining survey (arXiv 2509.02547) was published in TMLR. [source](https://mlanthology.org/tmlr/2026/zhang2026tmlr-landscape)

## 4. Base rates
All counts below were taken on 2026-11-01 with the resolution query. Older windows are understated because later revisions move papers out of them.

| Window | Count today |
|---|---|
| Nov-Dec 2025 (the same period last year) | 106 (Nov 66, Dec 39) |
| Jan-Feb 2026 | 105 |
| Mar-Apr 2026 | 139 |
| May-Jun 2026 | 184 (Jun 79) |
| Jul-Aug 2026 | 144 (Jul 70, Aug 69) |
| Sep-Oct 2026 | 221 (Sep 79, Oct 138) |

- **Trend:** Two-month counts have roughly doubled over the year, from about 105 to 221. The rise is uneven: there was a summer dip, then a jump in October.
- **Possible conference effect:** The October page includes papers marked "Submitted to ICLR 2027" and "ICRA 2027". Conference deadlines may explain part of the October spike, and conference revisions could add to Nov-Dec. I did not check the conference dates.
- **Holiday dip:** December 2025 had about 40% fewer papers than November 2025 (39 vs 66), so late December tends to be slow.
- **Comparability:** Metaculus will count right after Dec 31. That is most like measuring Sep-Oct today (221), before later revisions shrink the window. Older windows are biased low compared with a fresh count.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-01: The market prices supplied with this question are all unrelated. The closest is Kalshi's Merriam-Webster word-of-the-year market, which has "Agentic" at 0.17. None of them bear on this count.
- My search found no Metaculus community forecast, Manifold market or expert forecast for this question. [source](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.02547)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Conference cycles:** Rebuttal revisions and camera-ready updates from conference deadlines in Nov-Dec could add revised versions to the count. I did not verify the dates.
- **Year-end lull:** Late-December holidays usually cut arXiv submissions.
- **Big releases:** Major lab model or agent-training releases often bring follow-up preprints. I could not identify any specific scheduled release.
- **Search changes:** Any change to arXiv's search indexing or matching would shift the count, since the current number depends on loose phrase matching.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-01: The Nov 1 to Dec 31, 2026 window can't be counted yet. I ran the question's exact search with other date ranges (date type `submitted_date`, cross-lists included). [arXiv search](https://arxiv.org/search/advanced?advanced=&terms-0-operator=AND&terms-0-term=%22agentic+reinforcement+learning%22&terms-0-field=abstract&classification-physics_archives=all&classification-include_cross_list=include&date-year=&date-filter_by=date_range&date-from_date=2026-10-01&date-to_date=2026-10-31&date-date_type=submitted_date&abstracts=hide&size=25&order=-submitted_date)

  - Oct 24 to 31: 29
- **How the search counts papers:** `submitted_date` appears to use the date of a paper's *latest version*. arXiv offers a separate `submitted_date_first` option for the original submission date. If that reading is right:
  - Revisions posted in Nov and Dec of older papers will add to the count.
  - Papers first posted in Nov or Dec but revised before Metaculus runs the search will drop out.
  - Evidence: one October result is a v2 revision (Alibaba "AgenticBigBang").
  - Using original submission dates instead gives Oct 2026: **91** (vs 138) and Sep 2026: **62** (vs 79).

Patterns worth noting:
- Last year, Nov plus Dec was about 2.1 times October (106 vs 51). Applying that ratio to Oct 2026 (138) would suggest roughly 290. This is only a rough guide: the term was spreading fast in late 2025, and that growth inflated the ratio.
- Simply doubling a typical 70 to 80 month from mid-2026 gives about 140 to 160. Running the October pace for two months gives about 275.
- Month-to-month swings are large, often 30 to 80%. They tend to follow conference cycles: May matches the NeurIPS deadline, and October follows the ICLR deadline.
- December 2025 was much lower than November (39 vs 67), likely the holiday slowdown.

- I found no Metaculus community forecast or expert forecast for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **November 2026:** ICLR 2027 author responses and paper revisions, which could add revised papers to the count. CVPR 2027 submissions are also likely around then (typical timing; I didn't check the date).
- **Early December 2026:** NeurIPS 2026 is expected (typical timing). Camera-ready versions and workshop papers could lead to new submissions and revisions.
- **Late December 2026:** the holiday slowdown. Last year December was about 40% below November.
- **January 2027:** Metaculus runs the search shortly after Dec 31. Any revision posted before then moves a paper out of the window, while revisions of older papers during Nov and Dec bring them in.
- Late in the window, a day's count may rise slightly as listings catch up. I couldn't confirm the size of any indexing lag, and arXiv started rate-limiting my requests (HTTP 429) near the end.

(e) **Historical variation:** Two-month counts have moved by about 20 to 40% between consecutive windows (105, 139, 184, 144, 221). Swings of plus or minus 25% are normal.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market or expert forecast on this count. The question creator's range is 100 to 500.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** arXiv tightens its phrase matching so that classic multi-agent RL papers stop matching. Only the true "agentic reinforcement learning" phrase would count, which could mean around 70 to 100 papers.
- **High:** A burst of agentic-RL releases from major labs, plus heavy conference revision traffic and possibly looser matching, pushes the total to 350 or more.
